items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: Cisco disclosed a critical flaw in the AMP feature of Secure Email Gateway allowing unauthenticated remote file write and root command execution; Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation. CERT-EU urges immediate patching.

items.title: ConnectWise turns off its SaaS-y backup, security, and management services to probe security SNAFU
items.summary: ConnectWise disabled SaaS backup, security and management services while investigating a security incident; Huntress alleges Microsoft 365 account takeovers linked to it.

items.title: ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Backup After Attackers Compromise Microsoft 365 Tenants
items.summary: ConnectWise disabled seven application identities, including ConnectWise Cloud Backup, after threat actors abused them to gain unauthorized access to customer Microsoft 365 tenants.

items.title: 2026-016: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab CE and EE
items.summary: GitLab fixed 24 issues in CE/EE 19.4.2, 19.3.4 and 19.2.8, including a critical unauthenticated remote code execution bug. CERT-EU advises upgrading self-managed instances, starting with internet-facing ones.

items.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
items.summary: Atlassian patched a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability affecting Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible and Fisheye Data Center products; CERT-EU recommends upgrading and reviewing access logs.

items.title: Ransomware pressure now reaches employees’ homes and families
items.summary: Semperis' 2026 Ransomware Risk Report (1,200 respondents) finds attackers threatened employees' family members or friends at 37% of victim organisations, extending coercion beyond the workplace.

items.title: Cyberattack on French supermarkets tells us more about food security than AI safety
items.summary: Politico examines a cyberattack on French supermarkets in which hackers remotely raised refrigerator temperatures, highlighting OT/IoT exposure in the food supply chain; attacker motives remain unclear.

items.title: Linux KVM guest-host escape rated critical, may represent a new way to attack penguin-powered networking
items.summary: A critical Linux KVM guest-to-host escape dubbed 'PwnEscape' is rated 9.3 and may open a new attack path against Linux-based networking and virtualised infrastructure.

items.title: Hackers exploit SiteGuard WAF flaw to run commands as admins
items.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting an OS command injection flaw in SiteGuard Server Edition WAF, enabling command execution as root or SYSTEM on affected servers.

items.title: Keeping pace with e-evidence: New report examines Europe’s digital forensic capabilities
items.summary: A European Commission/Europol-coordinated report finds EU digital forensic capabilities are struggling to keep pace with the volume and diversity of e-evidence generated by modern technologies.

items.title: Half the AI bot traffic hammering your website comes from Meta
items.summary: DataDome reports AI agent traffic grew 41.5% QoQ to nearly 25 billion requests in Q3 2026, with Meta accounting for about half; 99.3% of sampled Muse traffic came from cloud/CDN infrastructure.

items.title: Trump’s Russia rethink — and Europe’s response
items.summary: Politico analyses how EU capitals are responding to Trump's shifting stance on Russia and Ukraine, and what it means for Kyiv.

items.title: Ukraine launches over 1,000 drones at Russia, setting oil facilities ablaze
items.summary: Ukraine launched over 1,000 drones at Russian targets, setting oil facilities ablaze in one of its largest strikes of the war.

items.title: 5 fights that will shape NATO’s next Russia war plans
items.summary: NATO allies begin negotiating new military requirements and war plans amid growing fears of confrontation with Russia.

items.title: Orphaned VBA Projects Inside DWG Files: YARA Rule, (Sun, Oct 18th)
items.summary: SANS ISC published a YARA rule to detect orphaned VBA projects embedded inside AutoCAD DWG files, a potential malware delivery vector.

items.title: Ukrainian forces strike St Petersburg and Leningrad region
items.summary: Ukrainian forces struck St Petersburg and the Leningrad region, while Russia targeted Ukraine's energy sector across four regions, killing two people.

items.title: US Cybersecurity Job Postings Fall 26% as AI Security Engineer Demand Soars
items.summary: CyberSN's report shows US cybersecurity job postings down 26% while demand for AI security engineers rises sharply.

items.title: Week in review: Hidden implant in Ledger wallets linked to $93M theft, 1,500+ npm packages exposed
items.summary: Weekly roundup covering a hidden implant in Ledger wallets tied to a $93M theft, 1,500+ exposed npm packages, and AWS's Strands Box sandbox for AI agents.

items.title: Bearer CLI: Free, source-available code security scanning tool (SAST)
items.summary: Bearer CLI is a free, source-available SAST tool that scans code without executing it and prioritises findings by the sensitivity of the data they touch.

items.title: More than 200 arrested in second day of street clashes against cost of living in Milan
items.summary: Over 200 people were arrested during a second day of cost-of-living street clashes in Milan; PM Meloni called a security meeting on the violence.

items.title: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
items.summary: President Macron addressed the nation calling for 'calm and order' after widespread disorder and continued looting in Paris.

items.title: RPO and RTO explained with a real disaster recovery example
items.summary: A Help Net Security video explains the practical difference between RPO and RTO, stressing that backups alone do not guarantee fast recovery of usable data.

items.title: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to 'public benefit fund'
items.summary: Anthropic said it will commit 5% of its shares to a 'public benefit fund' as it prepares for a potential stock market listing.

items.title: France's government under pressure after weekend of widespread violence
items.summary: France's government faces political pressure after a weekend of rioting during cost-of-living and public services protests.

items.title: AI giant Anthropic commits 5% of shares to ‘public benefit’ fund
items.summary: Anthropic says its new public benefit fund, backed by 5% of shares, could support NGO donations and direct distributions to populations.

items.title: Trump defends Russian sanctions relief, lashes out at Zelenskyy
items.summary: Trump defended sanctions relief for Russia and criticised Zelenskyy, as Kyiv held talks with US envoys.

items.title: Putin proposes summit with Trump and Xi to discuss Ukraine deal, WSJ says
items.summary: WSJ reports Putin has proposed a summit with Trump and Xi to discuss a Ukraine deal.

items.title: Bomb threat forces Israel to Austria flight into emergency landing
items.summary: A bomb threat forced an Israel-to-Austria flight to make an emergency landing in Bulgaria; all passengers and crew were unharmed.

items.title: The EU heads into a perfect political storm
items.summary: Analysis of EU political deadlock after last week's summit, suggesting difficulty reaching agreement on the budget and other files.

items.title: EU liberal chief urges conservatives to shun far right ahead of big election year
items.summary: The European Parliament's liberal group is making support for any Commission presidential candidate conditional on a coalition deal excluding the far right.

items.title: Russian strike kills woman, hits Kyiv subway station, mayor says
items.summary: A Russian strike hit a Kyiv subway station and killed a woman, according to the city's mayor.

items.title: Macron vows ‘full transparency’ in France after protests turn to widespread unrest
items.summary: Macron promised 'full transparency' and accountability for looters and rioters after French protests escalated into widespread unrest.

items.title: Macron vows to hold those who sought to 'bring down the Republic' accountable after riots
items.summary: Macron vowed to hold accountable those who sought to 'bring down the Republic', as unrest sharpens political tensions before next year's presidential election.

items.title: Security Sunday: Russlands Angriffe im Schwarzen Meer – mit Moritz Brake
items.summary: Podcast episode discussing Russian attacks in the Black Sea with analyst Moritz Brake.

items.title: Tensions remain high in Paris after violent protests across France
items.summary: Tensions remained high in Paris with isolated fires and small gatherings a day after violent protests in several French cities.

items.title: Spain changes Ceuta patrol rules over ships' "innocent passage"
items.summary: Spain's Navy changed its patrol protocol for Moroccan vessels exercising 'innocent passage' near Ceuta and Melilla, allowing action without higher authorisation.

items.title: Magyar links French riots to migration, says ‘shocking scenes’ justify hard line
items.summary: Hungary's Peter Magyar cited the French riots to justify a hard line on migration, echoed by Poland's Tusk; critics accused him of exploiting the unrest.

items.title: Cost-of-living protests: 50 detained in Milan, clashes in Turin and Bologna
items.summary: About 50 people were detained in Milan after clashes during cost-of-living protests, with tensions also reported in Turin and Bologna.

items.title: OnlyFans Creators Are Pissed That Meta Lets Muse Talk Dirty
items.summary: Adult content creators criticise Meta for allowing its Muse AI agent to engage in sexual conversation while restricting their own accounts, raising AI content governance questions.

items.title: Data Centers Have a New PR Plan: Your Kid’s Field Trip
items.summary: Industry-aligned groups are running PR campaigns, including school field trips, to counter public backlash against data centre expansion.
